guide.title: Guide
guide.sub: How summoning works, where orbs come from, what each currency is for and which heroes are strong. Written for players who do not pay. As of 15 November 2026, game version 10.11.
guide.start.1: This site answers five questions: which heroes are strong, how to build a hero, which banner deserves your orbs, where each currency is best spent, and where it comes from.
guide.start.3: - Mark the heroes you own. The game does not let any site read your account, so nothing here fills in by itself.
guide.start.4: - Open Summon and enter your orbs. Each running banner then shows which focus heroes are new for you and whether a free pick is within reach.
guide.start.5: - Open a hero to see what kind of hero it is, how to get it and how to build it.
guide.start.6: - Save your barracks to a file now and then. It lives only in this browser.
guide.start.7: ## Three rules that save the most orbs
guide.start.8: - Summon on few banners and go to 40 summons where a free pick waits. A few summons on every banner rarely hit.
guide.start.9: - Collect what ends first. Orbs from story maps wait for you; orbs from quests and events are gone when the event ends.
guide.start.10: - Spend orbs on summoning only. Stamina, Arena tries and revives all have their own free items.
guide.summon.1: Orbs decide which heroes you get, so most planning is about them.
guide.summon.3: - A circle shows five stones. The first costs 5 orbs, the next three 4 each, the last 3: 20 orbs for all five.
guide.summon.4: - The first summon on every banner is free. A First Summon Ticket pays the first stone of a circle as well.
guide.summon.5: - Taking only the stones of one color is called sniping. It costs more per summon, up to 5 orbs each, but spends nothing on colors you do not want.
guide.summon.7: - New Heroes, their revivals, and event banners (Tempest Trials, Voting Gauntlet, Hall of Forms, Skill, New Power): 3% focus, 3% other 5-star heroes.
guide.summon.8: - Weekly Revival, Legendary Revival, Mythic Revival: 4% focus, 2% other.
guide.summon.10: - Double Special Heroes, New Heroes Return, Remix, A Hero Rises: 6% focus, no other 5-star heroes.
guide.summon.11: - Legendary, Mythic and Emblem banners and the anniversary's 12 Luminaries: 8% focus, no other 5-star heroes, twelve focus heroes.
guide.summon.12: - Every banner also has a 3% chance of a 4-star special rate hero: an older 5-star hero that arrives at 4 stars.
guide.summon.13: These numbers come from banner pages of 2025 and 2026. The banner's details screen in the game always has the last word.
guide.summon.15: - Every five summons without a 5-star hero add 0.5% to the 5-star rate. The raise is applied when you finish the circle.
guide.summon.16: - After 120 summons without a 5-star hero, every stone of the next circle is a 5-star hero.
guide.summon.17: - A 5-star focus hero sets the rate back to the start. A 5-star that is not a focus hero lowers the raise but does not remove it. A 4-star hero changes nothing.
guide.summon.18: - The raise belongs to one banner. It does not move to the next.
guide.summon.20: - After 40 summons on a banner you choose one of its 5-star focus heroes for free. The free first summon and ticket summons count.
guide.summon.21: - For everyone: New Heroes, Revival, New Heroes Return, Legendary/Mythic/Emblem Hero Remix, and the Legendary and Mythic weekly revivals.
guide.summon.22: - Only with Feh Pass (paid): Special Heroes on their first run, Double Special Heroes, Legendary, Mythic and Emblem banners, Hero Fest.
guide.summon.23: - Forty summons cost at most 155 orbs with full circles: eight circles of 20, minus the free first stone. Sniping one color can cost up to 195.
guide.summon.24: - Each free pick also gives one Celestial Stone.
guide.summon.26: - A banner with a free pick for everyone, when you want one of its heroes and can reach 40 summons: one copy is certain.
guide.summon.27: - A Legendary, Mythic or Emblem banner when one color holds two or three heroes you lack: every 5-star of that color is then likely a win. With one wanted hero among three in a color, two of three 5-stars miss.
guide.summon.28: - Free Summon and Select Summon banners cost nothing. Take them first.
guide.summon.30: - A few summons on every banner.
guide.summon.31: - Merges of a new 5-star hero. Every further copy costs as much as the first.
guide.summon.32: - Event banners at 3% without a free pick, unless you want exactly that hero.
guide.summon.33: Keep 155 orbs in reserve when you can. That is one finished free pick whenever a hero you really want appears.
guide.orbs.1: Orbs come from things you do once and from things that return.
guide.orbs.3: - Story maps and Paralogues: orbs for the first clear of each map on each difficulty. For a new account this is the biggest stock by far.
guide.orbs.4: - Chain Challenges, Squad Assault, Tactics Drills and Blessed Gardens: more one-time orbs, harder to get. Come back when your teams are stronger.
guide.orbs.5: These orbs never expire. Leave them for a month with little else.
guide.orbs.7: - Monthly quests and training quests. In November 2026 they hold 17 orbs.
guide.orbs.8: - Quests of the running events and of returning Grand Hero Battles.
guide.orbs.9: - Tempest Trials, once a month: orbs on the score ladder.
guide.orbs.10: - Log-in bonuses that come with new banners and events.
guide.orbs.12: - Arena: one orb for the first win of the season, and more with the tier reward at the end of the week.
guide.orbs.14: Aether Raids pays no orbs. It pays Aether Stones, Heroic Grails, Dragonflowers, Divine Codes and Blessings.
guide.orbs.15: Feh Pass has its own quests with 5 orbs twice a month. They are paid and are counted separately on this site.
guide.orbs.16: The Orbs page lists what is still open, soonest end first.
guide.spend.1: What each currency is for, where it comes from and what to do with it. Advice marked as experience is the author's judgement as a long-time player.
guide.spend.3: - For: raising a hero's rarity. 4 to 5 stars costs 20,000.
guide.spend.4: - From: Arena every week, quests (6,800 in the November 2026 quests), events, and sending home heroes you do not need.
guide.spend.5: - Best use (experience): 5 stars for heroes from the 3 to 4-star pool that you really field, then their merges.
guide.spend.7: - For: copies of heroes from Grand Hero Battles and Tempest Trials. The first copy of a hero costs 100, each further one 50 more, up to 500. Eleven copies, enough for +10, cost 3,700.
guide.spend.8: - From: Aether Raids (daily, tier and rank rewards) and quests.
guide.spend.9: - Best use (experience): take one hero to +10 before starting a second.
guide.spend.11: - For: extra stats. Five steps give +1 to every stat. There is one kind per movement type. They do not change Arena scoring.
guide.spend.12: - From: Heroic Ordeals (one map for every hero you own), Aether Raids every week, Allegiance Battles and quests.
guide.spend.13: - Best use (experience): the first five steps on each hero of your main teams. Older heroes can take more steps than new ones.
guide.spend.15: - For: Combat Manuals, which work like a copy of a hero for merging or passing on skills.
guide.spend.16: - Part codes (now Part 7) come from the tier and rank rewards of Arena, Aether Raids and Mjölnir's Strike.
guide.spend.17: - Ephemera codes come from events and are lost when their time is up. Each number is handed out for about six weeks. Spend them first.
guide.spend.18: ## Refining Stones, Divine Dew and Arena Medals
guide.spend.19: - For: the Weapon Refinery. Common weapons cost Refining Stones and Arena Medals. Personal weapons cost Divine Dew and Arena Medals.
guide.spend.20: - From: Arena, quests and events. Every Refining Stone you spend gives one Divine Dew back, and that is the main source of Dew.
guide.spend.21: - Best use (experience): Dew on the personal weapons of heroes in your teams. A refine often makes an old hero useful again.
guide.spend.23: - For: creating and upgrading Sacred Seals.
guide.spend.24: - From: Arena, Arena Assault, Tempest Trials, Voting Gauntlet and quests.
guide.spend.26: - Aether Stones build and improve the structures of your Aether Raids keep. From: Aether Raids, quests, and the Aether Resort.
guide.spend.27: - Every Aether Stone you spend gives one Heavenly Dew. Heavenly Dew strengthens the two Fortresses and the resource structures.
guide.spend.28: ## Items that come with a hero
guide.spend.29: - Aide's Essence (from each Aided hero): +1 to all stats for another hero.
guide.spend.30: - Bouquet (from each Entwined hero): support rank S+ for another hero.
guide.spend.31: - Vignette (from each Vista hero): +2 to all stats for another hero. Heroes from versions at least two numbers back can take a second one, for +4.
guide.spend.32: - Ascendant Floret (from the first copy of each Ascended hero, and some quests): a second asset for another hero.
guide.spend.33: - Celestial Stone (one with every free pick): exchanged in the Celestial Stone Shop.
guide.spend.34: These items are part of what a summon is worth. They are not used up by time, so give them to heroes you will keep using.
guide.spend.35: ## Do not spend orbs on these
guide.spend.36: - Stamina Potions restore stamina, Dueling Crests restore Arena tries, Light's Blessings revive a team. The game offers an orb in their place when you run out. Decline.
guide.spend.37: The Currencies page has one card for each of these with its sources.
guide.meta.1: Which heroes are strongest changes every month. This site does not rate heroes. It gives you three things: facts from the game data on every hero page, a short dated list of picks, and a link to the tier list on Game8.
guide.meta.3: - Newer beats older on stats. Melee infantry heroes released in 2017 have 158 stat points on average; those of 2021 have 179; those of 2026 have 205.
guide.meta.4: - The stat total is not strength. 33 of the 40 highest totals belong to armored heroes. The total matters for Arena scoring, where a higher total brings stronger opponents and more points.
guide.meta.5: - Compare a hero with others of the same movement and weapon. The hero page shows where its stats stand in that group.
guide.meta.7: - Legendary heroes boost allies who carry the matching blessing during their season. Mythic heroes do the same in Aether Raids and decide how much Lift you win or lose there.
guide.meta.8: - An Emblem hero engages with one other hero and strengthens that hero. This also works on defence and does not change Arena scores.
guide.meta.9: - A Chosen hero grants powers to one hero in Arena, Arena Assault and Allegiance Battles.
guide.meta.10: - Aided, Entwined and Vista heroes hand an item to another hero with every copy. See Other currencies.
guide.meta.12: The picks are heroes that two independent tier lists both place at the top on the given date. No ratings are copied. For the full, current rating follow the link to Game8.
guide.about.1: Heroes Companion is a free fan project. It is not affiliated with Nintendo or Intelligent Systems. Fire Emblem Heroes and all its names belong to their owners.
guide.about.3: - Heroes, stats, skills, builds, banners and rewards: the Fire Emblem Heroes Wiki (feheroes.fandom.com). Its text and data are under a Creative Commons licence; the build descriptions are the wiki authors' words.
guide.about.4: - Level 40 stats are calculated from the wiki's level 1 stats and growth rates for a 5-star hero with a neutral nature.
guide.about.5: - Summoning rules: the rates boxes of the wiki's banner pages from 2025 and 2026, and the official Feh Pass page for the free pick. Each rule carries its source and date.
guide.about.6: - Ratings and tier lists are not copied. Game8 does not allow reuse of its data, so hero pages link to it instead.
guide.about.8: - Your barracks, teams and orb count are stored in your browser only. Nothing is sent to a server, there is no account and no tracking.
guide.about.10: - The data is as old as the date at the bottom of the page. The game changes every month; new heroes appear after the next data update.
guide.about.11: - Where the data is missing, the page says so. It does not guess.
guide.about.12: - The Standing block describes a hero. It is not a rating.

about.art.title: Artwork
about.art.1: Fire Emblem Heroes, its characters and all hero artwork (portraits, battle art, map sprites) are © Nintendo / INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS. Each illustration was drawn by the artist named on the hero's page. This site is unofficial fan content, carries no advertising and earns nothing.
about.art.2: Hero artwork is not stored on this site. Your browser loads it from the image host of the Fire Emblem Heroes Wiki. The switch "Show game artwork" in the footer turns it off; the site then shows its own silhouette instead and requests nothing from that host.
about.art.issues: Open the project's issue page on GitHub
about.art.3: The emblem, textures, frames, the summoning circle and the weapon and movement icons are original images made for this site. If you hold rights to any artwork shown here and want it removed, open an issue on the project's repository page; it will be removed without discussion.
about.data.title: Data and licence
about.data.1: Hero, skill, banner and quest data come from the Fire Emblem Heroes Wiki; its text and data are licensed {licence}. Build texts are the wiki authors' words and link to their source page.
